title: read_dot_stuffed: LF-only articles are silently normalized to CRLF, changing CID
description: session.rs read_dot_stuffed (line 558-567) reconstructs each line as format\!('{trimmed}\r\n'), where trimmed has CRLF stripped. For an article sent with LF-only line endings (RFC 3977 permits both), this converts every line to CRLF before storing to IPFS. The CID computed from the stored bytes will differ from a CID computed by any other peer from the wire bytes. Trigger: peer sends IHAVE/TAKETHIS with an LF-only article body. Bad behavior: the stored CID cannot be used to verify article integrity against the wire representation; two transit nodes receiving the same LF-only article will produce the same CID (both normalize to CRLF), but the article as stored does not match what was sent. More critically: the X-Stoa-Sig verification (verify/x_sig.rs) operates on original_bytes (before pipeline modifications) while the pipeline modifies the bytes further (prepend_path_header). The signer signs pre-pipeline bytes; the signature check is against original_bytes which is post-normalization. This is internally consistent but callers who verify against wire bytes will see a mismatch.
